summary: George A. Kennedy was a scholar in sinology and linguistics. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin under Erich Haenisch and Otto Franke (~1932–1935), later holding a post at Yale University (~1935–1960).

Keyworth works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara under Ronald Egan, William F. Powell, and Shuizhao Wang, and earned his PhD at UCLA under Robert E. Buswell Jr. He held posts at CU Boulder and Saskatchewan.

George Abraham Grierson was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Trinity College Dublin (~1868–1871). He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1871–1898), as Superintendent of the Linguistic Survey of India (1898–1928), and as Governor at SOAS (1917–1925).
George C. O. Haas was an Indologist. He served as Recording Secretary for the American Oriental Society (~1914–1918) and was an editor for the Journal of the American Oriental Society (~1916–1918).

George Cardona worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at NYU and Yale, under Warren Crawford Cowgill and Paul Thieme, as well as traditional teachers in India. He was a long-time professor at the University of Pennsylvania (~1965–2004).

George Chemparathy is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Erich Frauwallner (~1966–1969) and Paul Hacker. He held posts at Loyola College, Chennai, and as a professor at Utrecht University (~1974–1993).

George Cowgill was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Harvard University (~1956–1963). He held academic posts at Brandeis University (~1960–1990) and Arizona State University (~1990–2010).
George Croom Robertson was a philosopher who studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1857–1861) and University College London. He held a post at University College London (~1866–1892).

George Cœdès studied Indology, sinology, and history at EPHE under Finot, Lévi, and Foucher. He was director of the EFEO (1929–1947), led the National Library of Thailand (1918–1929), and taught at INALCO and the Sorbonne.

George D. Bond is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at the University of Sri Lanka and earned his PhD at Northwestern University (~1968–1972), where he served as Professor of Religion (~1974–2012).

George David Birkhoff studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University. He held academic posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1907–1909), Princeton University (1909–1912), and Harvard University (1912–1944).

George Derwent Thomson worked in philosophy and linguistics. He studied at King's College, Cambridge (~1922–1926) and Trinity College Dublin (~1926–1927), and held posts at the University of Cambridge (~1927–1936) and the University of Birmingham (~1937–1970).

George Devereux studied at INALCO, the Faculty of Arts of Paris, UC Berkeley, and under Marcel Mauss (~1930–1933). He later held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1963–1985) and Paris Descartes University (~1970–1985).

George E. Dunkel is a linguist and Indologist who earned his doctorate at the University of Pennsylvania (~1971–1976). He held posts at Johns Hopkins University (1975–1978), Princeton University (1978–1986), and the University of Zurich (1986).

George Foot Moore was a religious studies scholar who studied at Yale and Union Theological Seminary. He was a professor at Andover Theological Seminary (1883–1902) and Frothingham Professor of the history of religion at Harvard University (1904–1928).

George Frederick Baumann is an Indologist who earned his PhD at Heidelberg University (~1968–1973) and studied at Bibliothekar-Lehrinstitut des Landes Nordrhein-Westfalen. He held posts at the University of Tübingen and its library (~1975/1976–2001).
George Herbert Palmer was a philosopher who studied at Phillips Academy (~1856–1860) and Harvard University (~1860–1864). He subsequently held a faculty post at Harvard University (~1870–1913).

George L. Hart is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. After earning a PhD in Sanskrit at Harvard University (~1965–1971), he taught at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1969–1975) and served as a professor at UC Berkeley (~1975–2014).

George Lakoff is a linguist and philosopher who studied at MIT and earned his doctorate at Indiana University. He taught linguistics at Harvard University (1965–1969) and served as a professor of linguistics at UC Berkeley (1972–2016).

George Melville Bolling was an Indologist and linguist who earned his doctorate at Johns Hopkins University. He held professorships at the Catholic University of America (1895–1913) and Ohio State University (1914–1939), and served as president of the Linguistic Society of America (1931).
